measure_bench.name: Measure Bench
measure_bench.description: One body, eight measures of it, and the question none of the four members answers: how does a quantity get its metre? A 0.240 x 0.915 x 0.180 m slab stands on a one-metre plate beside a post that is two rulers at once - a graduated SI metre from the plate top to exactly 1.000 m, and above it, unticked and in Le Corbusier's red, the Modulor's raised hand at 2.26 m drawn at 1:2. The slab is squeezed once at navel height and that squeeze is identical in all twenty-four cells; nothing about the body is a variable. Each measure is real geometry at true scale: velocity and acceleration as rods whose length IS the quantity at ForceMagnitudeDemo's own 0.33 m per unit - 0.660 m of acceleration against 0.066 m of velocity, ten to one, and the whole of the ratio is 0.1 s of clock; collision as twenty-four 0.030 m arrows at the softbody's saturating 0.020 m per m/s; strain as the softbody's own diamonds, 0.008 to 0.020 m, scaled by a ratio with no denominator; volume as two cubes of side V^(1/3), the current one 38 percent larger than the rest one because the member measures volume as a bounding box; and the Modulor as datum lines and a Vitruvian frame at a flat 1:2. Then `reading` asks each of them for the time window it took, and six of the eight draw nothing - including acceleration, whose name is a derivative and whose code is division.
dev_themes: what a quantity has to be divided by before it can be drawn
interactions: stand at reading=alone and walk the measure axis: the rods are all lengths, and nothing on the bench tells you they are lengths in different currencies. 0.660 m of acceleration and 0.030 m of collision arrow are the same kind of mark and mean nothing like the same thing

put velocity beside acceleration under reading=on: same colour family, same origin, same 0.33 m per unit, and one is ten times the other purely because 0.1 s passed between them. That ratio is the family's scale factor doing its work in public

walk the whole measure axis at reading=window and watch six of eight cells draw nothing at all. That is not a broken capture - it is pre-registered in designed_nulls. acceleration draws nothing because a = F/m is algebra at an instant
look for the one value that does have a window: collision, whose (current - prev) / delta is the only finite difference anywhere in the family, drawn as the two sampled positions 0.025 m apart at 1:1

stand at measure=volume and notice the wire cage is BIGGER than the grey cube inside it. The body was squeezed and the reported volume went UP 38 percent, because the member computes volume as the product of bounding-box extents and the bulge is wider than the dent is deep
read the post: it is graduated for one metre and smooth above it. A metre is divided, a canon is not
measure_bench.capacity: SEE that `measure` is not one question but a bundle of unstated divisions - that before any quantity can be drawn as geometry something must be chosen as its metres-per-unit, that ForceMagnitudeDemo makes that choice once and spends it on three different dimensions without saying so, and that the two words in the family which sound like derivatives take no limit while the one that sounds like a state takes the only one

spatial_needs.footprint_note: The STAGE is the footprint and it is drawn before either axis is consulted: a 1.00 x 0.68 m plate and, at x = -0.44, a post running from the plate top to y = 1.154. The drawn figure moves a long way inside that box - the acceleration rod reaches x = +0.500, the volume cage reaches z = +0.190, the canon circle reaches y = 1.154, and in the window reading six of eight cells contain nothing but the body and the post - while the world box stays 1.000 x 1.154 x 0.680 in all twenty-four cells. That is why the stage exists, and why the post is in every cell rather than only in the ones that need a reference. layout=ladder stands all eight measures in a row at 1.20 m pitch, about 8.4 m wide, and is a design view rather than a map placement.

measurements.source: computed_from_geometry in a Python replica built from the same constants; no Godot was run. The box is the STAGE and nothing else: the plate spans x +-0.50 and z +-0.34, and the tallest thing in every cell is the post's red extension at y = 1.154, which is the Modulor's 2.26 m at 1:2 and is also exactly where the canon circle's top lands. The drawn body's own extent runs 0.240 x 0.9293 x 0.2454 under the one squeeze - 0.240 x 0.915 x 0.180 at rest - and it is IDENTICAL IN ALL TWENTY-FOUR CELLS, which is what makes the AABB identical by construction rather than by luck.

dna.default: measure=none, reading=on. `none` is the default because it is the one value all three vocabularies contain - the softbody's `none` (the four ImmediateMeshes cleared, the arithmetic upstream untouched, 'what a specimen looks like when nobody is reading it', in its own comment) and modulor_man_demo's `body`, whose branch is `if measure == "body": return` and builds nothing at all. It is also the honest default for a bench whose subject is the instrument rather than the specimen: the first thing to see is the body, the plate and the metre post, with no quantity laid over them. `on` is the default because it is the family's own condition - every member draws its measure on its subject, in place, and none of them ever draws the measure alone or shows the window it took. NOTE WHAT THIS COSTS: the default cell is the plainest tile in the sheet, and the closest pre-registered pair is measured against it. That is deliberate. It is the cell every other cell is a departure from, so the departures are what get measured, and the framing is set by the stage rather than by the figure so the camera does not move when the figure does.
dna.note:
WHAT THE VALUES MEAN, where each came from, whether it is a DERIVATIVE, a STATE or a CANON, and - the part this bench exists for - HOW MANY METRES OF GEOMETRY IT DRAWS PER UNIT OF QUANTITY.

THE FAMILY FIRST, as a census before it is an argument. Four artifacts declare an axis called `measure`, in three vocabularies, eleven words: ForceMagnitudeDemo says both | acceleration | velocity | none; rounded_softbody and rounded_softbody_test both say strain | collision | volume | none; modulor_man_demo says body | scale | canon | module | crowd.

THE TWO SOFTBODY NAMES ARE NOT ONE SCENE, and the brief's guess needs correcting in a specific direction. They are TWO scenes, NESTED: rounded_softbody_test.tscn instances rounded_softbody.tscn as a child called `RoundedSoftBody` and adds a floor and a cube to fall onto. Its root script rounded_softbody_test.gd owns nothing, builds nothing and draws nothing - it is a pass-through that re-declares the same four-value enum and forwards config down. So the relation is ONE IMPLEMENTATION UNDER TWO NAMES, which is the corpus's one-scene-many-names pattern in its nested form, and the tell here is not identical export counts (the harness has one export, the specimen has seven) but a comment in the harness that reads 'Kept identical to rounded_softbody.gd's list, character for character.' Both files record WHY: the harness root used to carry no script at all, so GridInteractablesComponent - which sets config_* metadata on the ROOT and calls apply_grid_config on the ROOT - fell through for all eight placements, and any axis declared on the child would have been declared-but-unreachable from a map token. Two names, one enum, one implementation, and the second name exists to make the first reachable.

THE THING THE CODE SAYS THAT THE BRIEF DID NOT, and it is the finding. The brief said velocity and acceleration are DERIVATIVES, which do not exist at an instant without a limit, so drawing them requires choosing a time window. FORCEMAGNITUDEDEMO TAKES NO LIMIT ANYWHERE. `velocity` is `physics_ball.linear_velocity / SCENE_SCALE` - the engine's number, read off the server, not this file's - and `acceleration` is `force_logical / _mass`, a division. There is no difference quotient, no previous frame, no window, in either branch of that file. THE ONE GENUINE DERIVATIVE IN THE FAMILY IS `collision`, in the softbody: `var vel: Vector3 = (current - prev) / maxf(delta, 0.001)`, a finite difference over one physics tick, thresholded at speed > 1.5, with markers decaying at `delta * 2.0` - a 0.5 s display window on top of a tick-length measurement window. The word that sounds like a state is the only one that takes a limit; the two words that sound like derivatives take none. So the axis does NOT span derivative / state / canon in the way the brief laid out, and the labels below are the code's, not the brief's.

AND THE DECISIVE FACT. Every rod ForceMagnitudeDemo draws is scaled by one constant: `const SCENE_SCALE: float = 0.33` (vector_scene_base.gd:10), applied as `end_node.position = vector * SCENE_SCALE` (:141) to the force arrow, the velocity arrow and the acceleration arrow alike. FORCE IN NEWTONS, VELOCITY IN METRES PER SECOND AND ACCELERATION IN METRES PER SECOND SQUARED ARE ALL DRAWN AT 0.33 m PER UNIT. Three dimensions, one ruler, never declared anywhere in the file, the base class or the registry. The brief asked this bench to state its metres-per-unit because putting a derivative and a state on one bench requires choosing it. The family already chose - silently, three times over - and that choice is the reason one of its two 'derivatives' is nearly invisible beside the other.

MEASURE, eight values. At least one from each vocabulary, `none` included, and every scale factor lifted from a member unless marked DERIVED.

  none - THE NULL, and the one value all three vocabularies contain. rounded_softbody's `none` clears its four ImmediateMeshes and lets the strain, the collisions and the volume drift go on being computed and not drawn; modulor_man_demo's `body` returns before building its host node, so 'the legacy lineage builds nothing at all'. Same value, two names, and modulor's name collides with ForceMagnitudeDemo's OTHER axis, where `body` means the mass being pushed (light 0.25 kg | standard 1.0 | heavy 4.0 | immovable 16.0). NO KIND, NO SCALE FACTOR - the body, the plate and the metre, and nothing laid over them.

  velocity - ForceMagnitudeDemo. NOT A DERIVATIVE IN THIS CODE: read off physics_ball.linear_velocity, the engine's integral, and divided by SCENE_SCALE to get back to logical units. SCALE FACTOR 0.330 m PER m/s, which is SCENE_SCALE. The quantity drawn is the speed the demo's own ball has reached at its own first readout: a = F/m = 2.0 / 1.0 from the initial force Vector3(2.0, 0, 0) and the base class's const BALL_MASS = 1.0, over the demo's own const UPDATE_INTERVAL = 0.1 s, so v = 0.200 m/s and the rod is 0.0660 m. Every number in that sentence is the member's; the one multiplication is this bench's and is the only arithmetic here the member does not do itself.

  acceleration - ForceMagnitudeDemo. NOT A DERIVATIVE EITHER: `force_logical / _mass`, algebra at an instant, no limit taken. SCALE FACTOR 0.330 m PER m/s^2 - THE SAME NUMBER AS VELOCITY'S, for a different dimension, which is the whole point. |a| = 2.00 m/s^2 draws 0.6600 m of rod, and 0.660 leaving the body's face at x = -0.160 lands at x = +0.500, the plate's own edge. TEN TIMES THE VELOCITY ROD, and the entire ratio is 0.1 s of clock. Two quantities that the member draws in the same colour family, from the same origin, on the same ruler, differing by a factor of ten for a reason that is not about the ball.

  collision - rounded_softbody. THE ONLY TRUE DERIVATIVE IN THE FAMILY, and it carries the only real time window: (current - prev) / delta. SCALE FACTOR 0.020 m PER m/s AND IT SATURATES: `arrow_len = 0.1 * clampf(speed / 5.0, 0.1, 1.0)`, so above 5 m/s every arrow is 0.100 m whatever hit the body, and below 0.5 m/s every arrow is 0.010 m. A ruler with a ceiling and a floor. Drawn at the member's own threshold speed of 1.5 m/s, which gives magnitude 0.30 and an arrow of 0.0300 m, at twenty-four sites (MAX_COLLISION_DISPLAY) on the dented face, each with the member's 0.015 * magnitude burst diamond at 0.0045 m.

  strain - rounded_softbody. STATE, and the one value here with NO DENOMINATOR AT ALL. E = 0.5 * k * d^2 with k = _stiffness = 0.5 and d measured from the rest lattice; the diamond is `sz = 0.008 + t * 0.012` where t = E over `_max_strain`, A RUNNING MAXIMUM DECAYED AT 0.999 PER FRAME. SCALE FACTOR 0.012 m PER UNIT OF A RATIO, over a 0.008 m floor. The same body under the same squeeze draws the same picture whether the strain energies are microjoules or megajoules, because the largest one in the frame is always t = 1. On this bench the peak displacement is 0.07494 m and E_max is 0.00140 - and neither number is visible in the drawing, which is the criticism.

  volume - rounded_softbody. STATE, and the one scale factor that CHANGES DIMENSION. The member reports volume as `extents.x * extents.y * extents.z`, the product of bounding-box extents, and draws it as a wireframe box and a 120-frame strip chart. Here it is drawn as a LENGTH, the only way a volume can be: two cubes of side V^(1/3) standing on the plate, the rest volume solid and grey at 0.3406 m and the current volume as a wire cage at 0.3797 m. SCALE FACTOR 1 m PER (m^3)^(1/3), a cube root. THE CAGE IS BIGGER THAN THE CUBE INSIDE IT: rest bbox 0.240 x 0.915 x 0.180 = 0.039528 m^3, squeezed bbox 0.240 x 0.9293 x 0.2454 = 0.054730 m^3, ratio 1.3846. The body was squeezed and its reported volume went UP 38 percent, because the dent is 0.075 m deep in one small patch and the bulge widens the whole box by 0.065 m. The member's own deviation law paints that COL_VOLUME_BAD red, and it is right to.

  module - modulor_man_demo. CANON. The two series as datum lines running clean through the body and out past it in Le Corbusier's own two colours, with the Blue-series squares nested to the right - the member's own construction, at MOD_K = 0.5. SCALE FACTOR 0.500 m PER METRE, dimensionless, because a canon's quantity is already a length and needs no conversion at all. That is why it is the only scale factor on this bench a reader can undo in their head: double any height off the post and you have Le Corbusier's number.

  canon - modulor_man_demo. CANON. The Vitruvian frame at 1:2, and the coincidence is drawn rather than asserted: a square of side 0.915 m (the standing height) on the plate, and a circle centred on the navel at 0.565 m with radius 0.565, so its bottom touches the plate and its top lands at 1.1540 m - which is where the post's red extension ends, because 2 x 1.13 = 2.26. SCALE FACTOR 0.500 m PER METRE. The two canon values share a scale factor and differ in what they do with it: `canon` says proportion is discovered in the body, `module` says it is legislated out past it.

WHAT THE MEMBER'S MODULOR NUMBERS ACTUALLY ARE - the brief asked, and the answer is half yes. THE CONSTANTS ARE GENUINE: ARM_RAISED 2.26, STANDING 1.83, SOLAR_PLEXUS 1.40, NAVEL 1.13 are Le Corbusier's 1.83 m Modulor, and the canon's arithmetic (navel at 1.13, radius 1.13, top at 2.26) is exact and is drawn. THE TWO NAMED SERIES ARE NOT WHAT THEY ARE NAMED. Le Corbusier's RED series runs ..., 0.16, 0.27, 0.43, 0.70, 1.13, 1.83, ... and the BLUE series is exactly twice it, ..., 0.33, 0.53, 0.86, 1.40, 2.26. The member's `RED_SERIES` is [2.26, 1.83, 1.40, 1.13] - that is the two series INTERLEAVED (Blue, Red, Blue, Red), not the Red series. Its `BLUE_SERIES` is [0.86, 0.70, 0.46, 0.43, 0.27, 0.18], of which 0.86 is Blue, 0.70 and 0.43 and 0.27 are RED, and 0.46 and 0.18 ARE IN NEITHER SERIES: they are the figure's own limb dimensions, lifted out of _figure_points() where `shoulder := 0.46 / 2.0` and `hip := 0.18`. The canonical rungs in those two slots are 0.53 and 0.20. The ratios say the same thing: 0.86/0.70 = 1.229, which is right for a step of the interleaved series, but 0.70/0.46 = 1.522 and 0.46/0.43 = 1.070, and two consecutive steps must multiply to phi = 1.618 - these give 1.629 and 1.871. AND PHI IS NEVER COMPUTED ANYWHERE IN THE FILE: no division, no 1.618, no recurrence, just two typed lists, one of them part anatomy. The member's numbers are used here UNCHANGED, wrong rungs and all, because this bench is a photograph of the family and not a correction of it - the correction is this paragraph.

READING, three values, and it is THIS SYNTHESIS'S OWN AXIS. No member declares anything like it: ForceMagnitudeDemo's second axis is `body` (the mass being pushed), the softbody has no second axis, and modulor_man_demo has none either.

  on - the quantity drawn on the body, in place, at true scale. The family's own condition, and its limitation: a mark whose size you can only judge against the thing it is on.

  alone - THE BODY IS NOT BUILT. The plate, the metre post and the quantity's own geometry, nothing else. This is where a 0.660 m acceleration rod and a 0.030 m collision arrow can be compared as LENGTHS against a graduated metre, which is the only way to see that they are lengths in different currencies. Note what it does to the two canon values: the frame and the datums are entirely legible with no figure in them, which is the criticism of a canon stated as an image rather than as a sentence.

  window - THE TIME WINDOW THE QUANTITY NEEDED, built as the actual sampled positions, and nothing else about the quantity. The body stays so that no cell is blank. SIX OF THE EIGHT VALUES DRAW NOTHING HERE. `collision` draws its own window: the two sampled positions of all twenty-four sites, 1.5 / 60 = 0.0250 m apart at 1:1, the only scale factor on this bench that is not a conversion. `velocity` draws a BORROWED window in grey: linear_velocity is integrated by the engine, not by the artifact, so the window is real and is not the artifact's - 0.200 m/s over one 60 Hz tick is 0.00333 m, which is roughly the thickness of the mark that draws it, and it is pre-declared as nearly invisible rather than discovered as a fault. Everything else draws nothing: acceleration because F/m is algebra at an instant, strain and volume because they are read off the body as it stands, module and canon because they were decided before the body arrived, none because it draws nothing anywhere.

HOW THE SHEET IS PROTECTED FROM THE COLOUR TRAP. Every colour here is a member's - green and blue from ForceMagnitudeDemo's arrows, pink and yellow from the softbody's collision markers, its three-stop strain ramp and its three volume states, RED_INK and BLUE_INK and BONE from modulor_man_demo - and none of it is load-bearing. NO PAIR IN THIS SHEET IS SEPARATED BY HUE ALONE, because every pair also differs in how much geometry exists: the values draw 0, 1, 2, 24, 48, 265 and 1200-odd primitives respectively, at lengths from 0.0033 m to 0.660 m. There is also NO EMISSION ANYWHERE, and the members use plenty (modulor_man_demo's _lit() runs emission_energy_multiplier up to 1.6) - the critic measures luminance, so an emissive value would separate pairs by glow rather than by geometry, and this bench is an argument about lengths.

THE THESIS SOMEONE COULD DISAGREE WITH: `measure` is not a question about which quantity to show, it is an undeclared division, and the proof is that the family's own scale factor is one constant spent on three dimensions - so two of its values differ by a factor of ten for a reason that is about the clock rather than about the ball. THE DISAGREEMENT AVAILABLE, and it is fair: a reader can say that 0.33 is just a display gain, that nobody reads a VR arrow with a ruler, and that the arrow is meant to be felt rather than measured - the demo's own @identity says 'Magnitude is felt, not read'. The answer is that the same file prints 'Force: %.2f N' and 'Acceleration: %.2f m/s^2' side by side in a nine-line readout, so it is asking to be read; and that the cell where holding the thesis costs something is `velocity` under `on`, where a bench that thinks the family's scale factor is doing real work has to draw a rod 0.066 m long and let it be the closest thing in the sheet to drawing nothing at all.

predicted_degeneracy.pair: velocity against none, in the on reading
predicted_degeneracy.arithmetic:
Rasterised BEFORE ANY CAPTURE in the critic's own currency: the geometry rebuilt in Python from the same constants (same lattice, same squeeze, same stage, same rod lengths derived the same way), projected through capture_config_sweep's camera (yaw 0.62, pitch -0.26, framing 0.56 on the union AABB of all twenty-four variants, which is the STAGE at 1.000 x 1.154 x 0.680 and therefore identical in every cell), then measured the way artifact_dna_critic measures: crop to the subject box, grey, resize 160 x 160, mean of the hottest 5 percent.

THE CONTEXT IS THE `on` READING AND THE RANKING IS COMPUTED INSIDE IT. Frame width = D * 1.9 * framing = 1.6716 * 1.9 * 0.56 = 1.7785 m, so 3.1632 m^2 of frame. The stage projects to 1.2090 x 1.4069 = 1.70087 m^2, which is 53.8 percent of frame and is the crop; one of the critic's 25600 compared pixels is therefore 6.644e-5 m^2.

WHY THAT PAIR. Under `on`, `none` draws the body, the plate and the post; `velocity` draws those plus ONE ROD, 0.0660 m long and 0.036 m square, leaving the body's face at x = -0.160 at navel height. That rod is the entire difference between the two frames. Its screen silhouette is (0.066 * cos 0.62 + 0.036 * sin 0.62) wide by (0.036 * cos 0.26 + 0.036 * sin 0.62 * sin 0.26) tall = 0.07464 x 0.04017 = 0.002998 m^2, which is 45.1 of the 25600 compared pixels. The hottest-5-percent window is 1280 pixels, so the window cannot fill with changed pixels: 45.1 of 1280 are hot and the rest are zero. Contrast is green (0.30, 1.00, 0.30), Rec.709 luminance 0.8006, against the plate at 0.2000 - a separation of 0.60, discounted to 0.553 for the lighting the replica renders flat. 45.1 / 1280 * 0.553 = 1.95 percent.

IT IS A CLUSTER OF TWO AND THE ORDER IS AT RISK, WHICH IS SAID IN ADVANCE. `collision` against `none` in the same reading computes to 2.18 percent: twenty-four arrows and twenty-four burst diamonds total 0.007755 m^2 = 116.7 pixels, but at a much lower contrast (pink 0.4705 against the body's 0.7100, a separation of 0.239). More area, less contrast, and the two land 12 percent apart - well inside the replica's own error. Naming velocity-none as `the` closest pair without saying that collision-none is beside it would be the wave-8 miss repeated. THE PAIR IS THE CLUSTER; the registered number is velocity-none's.

IT IS ALSO A CLAIM ABOUT WHY. The two frames closest to the frame with no measure in it are the family's smallest-scaled quantity and its saturating one, and they are nearly invisible for two different arithmetic reasons - 0.200 m/s at 0.33 m per unit, and 1.5 m/s at 0.020 m per m/s under a clamp. That is the thesis measured rather than asserted.

THE PREDICTION IS A FLOOR, NOT A FORECAST. The replica has one light, flat shading, no shadows, no AO, no antialiasing and no emission, and every prior prediction in this corpus under-read by 1.5x to 6.7x. IF THE SWEEP COMES BACK BELOW 1.95 ON THE NAMED PAIR, STOP AND INVESTIGATE THE HARNESS BEFORE THE DESIGN: (a) tools/check_dna_declarations.py - a value the code cannot reach falls back to `none` and prints identical tiles, and `none` being the default makes that failure look exactly like a small honest difference; (b) _rejects.json - all three exports are String enums and Object.set() on a typed property of the wrong type is refused in SILENCE; (c) whether the sheet was captured with --max=24, because at build_dna_gallery's default cap of 9 the 8 x 3 cross product is trimmed from the tail of the LATER axis and `reading` collapses to [on] alone, which deletes every designed null and the whole window argument.

THE PAIR AT REAL RISK IS IN ANOTHER READING AND IS NOT THE REGISTERED NUMBER. In `window`, `velocity` differs from the six-value null class only by two grey marks 0.00333 m apart, which computes to about 0.23 percent - below the 0.5 percent this corpus treats as render noise. It is registered as a designed null below rather than as a prediction, because a borrowed window being indistinguishable from no window is the claim, not the measurement. If it comes back ABOVE 1 percent, the grey marks are doing more work than their arithmetic allows and the finding is about this bench's mark sizes rather than about ForceMagnitudeDemo.

designed_nulls.why: IDENTICAL BY CONSTRUCTION AND IT IS THE SHARPEST SENTENCE ON THE BENCH. `acceleration` is the value whose name is a derivative; `none` is the value that means no measure at all. In the window reading they are the same photograph to the byte, because ForceMagnitudeDemo computes acceleration as `force_logical / _mass` - a division, at an instant, with no previous frame and no limit anywhere in the file. A quantity that needs no window is indistinguishable from no quantity, when the window is what you asked for. Predicted 0.00 percent focus / 0.00 percent frame on the replica; anything above 0.5 percent is render noise, and anything above 2 percent means something is leaking the measure geometry into the window rig.

A STATE and a CANON, and one photograph. These are the two values in this sheet that are furthest apart in every other respect - strain draws 265 diamonds on the body's own surface at a scale with no denominator, canon draws a 0.915 m square and a 0.565 m circle on a back plane at a flat 1:2 - and under `window` they are the same frame, because neither of them was ever measured over an interval. Registered as the class null: whatever else separates a state from a canon, it is not the window, and a reading that asks only for the window collapses them.

The same null, second pair across the same divide, and registered separately because a null that held for one pair and broke for another would mean the measure geometry is reaching the window rig somewhere it must not. `volume` is the widest-drawing state on the bench - two cubes of side 0.3406 and 0.3797 m plus two wire cages - and `module` is ten datum lines running 0.98 m. Here they are the same photograph. If this one comes back non-zero while the strain-canon pair is zero, the fault is in _build_window's early return and not in the argument.

The pair that closes the triangle, inside the STATE kind. All three of these zeros must hold together; two zeros and one non-zero is arithmetically impossible for identical images and would be a fact about the harness rather than about the artifact - most likely an unsettled first tile, which is why the critic neutralises each frame's own corner. It is also the pair that makes the class claim falsifiable in the other direction: strain and volume are read off the same lattice by two different arithmetics, and if the window rig were leaking anything at all, it would leak here first.

THE ONE NULL HERE THAT IS NOT ZERO, AND IT IS THE CLAIM. `velocity` does draw something in the window reading - two grey marks on the rod's axis, 0.200 m/s over one 60 Hz tick = 0.00333 m apart, each 0.004 x 0.040 x 0.040 m - so this pair is not identical and must not measure 0.00. It computes to about 0.23 percent: roughly 20 of 25600 pixels at a luminance separation of 0.15, which is below the 0.5 percent this corpus treats as noise but above nothing. THE BORROWED WINDOW IS INDISTINGUISHABLE FROM NO WINDOW, which is exactly what it means to say that linear_velocity's interval belongs to the engine and not to the artifact. Above 1 percent and the grey marks are bigger than their arithmetic allows - a fact about this bench's mark sizes, not about ForceMagnitudeDemo, and the note says so in advance.

dna.designed_nulls_why: FIVE NULLS, ONE EQUIVALENCE CLASS, AND THE CLASS IS THE ARGUMENT. In the `window` reading, six of the eight values draw nothing at all - acceleration, strain, volume, module, canon and none - so they form a single class of fifteen mutually identical pairs, of which four are registered above as samples spanning every kind boundary the axis has (derivative-name against null, state against canon, state against state). A null across a whole class of values is not four spare checks; it is the distinction the axis has collapsed, drawn. What `measure` sorts its values by - which quantity, in which units, at which gain - turns out to be invisible to the one question that would separate a measurement from a decision, and only ONE of the eight values survives it: `collision`, whose (current - prev) / delta is the sole finite difference in four artifacts. The fifth null is the interesting edge: `velocity` is nearly in the class and must not be exactly in it, because its window exists and belongs to somebody else. If any of the four zeros comes back above 2 percent, nothing else in this sheet can be believed. If the fifth comes back at 0.00, the grey marks were not built and the sheet is silently missing its most delicate claim.
dna.fixture_why: The bench can stand all eight measures in a row (layout=ladder, 1.20 m pitch, about 8.4 m wide) but the SWEEP must see one at a time: capture_config_sweep unions the AABB across a spec's variants, so an eight-wide row in the same spec would frame every cell against eight and a half metres and photograph the 0.066 m velocity rod as a speck - which happens to be the exact fault the closest registered pair is about, so getting this wrong would produce a sheet that appears to confirm the thesis while measuring nothing. layout is an export and not an axis, and it ships at single, so the fixture is a belt over braces. WHAT IS NOT FIXTURED, AND WHY NOTHING NEEDS TO BE: there is no clock and no random number here, and that is a deliberate refusal rather than an absence. Two of the three sources are among the least still artifacts in the corpus - rounded_softbody runs a SoftBody3D through PhysicsServer3D every _process frame, awaits two process frames before it can even record a rest state, and would be a different mesh in every tile; ForceMagnitudeDemo applies a central force in _physics_process and the ball is somewhere else in every frame. Nothing here simulates. The whole figure is built synchronously inside _ready from arithmetic on constants - no _process, no Timer, no randf, no SoftBody3D, no NoiseTexture2D - so two builds of one value are the same mesh and the squeeze is the same squeeze in all twenty-four cells.
dna.kin: The four sources are the kin, and they are unusually far apart for a family - a 1 m glass containment in the vectors sequence, a compression bench in the softbodies directory, its own bare harness, and a 2.26 m line drawing of a man in the wavefunctions directory. What they share is one word. ForceMagnitudeDemo's truth line is 'You never feel position or velocity. You feel acceleration. Force is the only thing that reaches your body' - which is a claim about which measure is real, made by an artifact whose default value draws all of them at once. rounded_softbody's is 'strain is not damage - it is the body's memory of every force that has touched it, written in the displacement of every vertex from its rest position', which is a claim that a state is a history, made by an artifact that normalises that state against a decaying maximum so no history survives the drawing. modulor_man_demo's is 'a standard human is not a fact about humans. It is a decision about which ones the building will fit' - the only one of the three that already knows its measure is a decision, which is why its two values are the two on this bench with an honest scale factor. A room holding this bench beside ForceMagnitudeDemo is saying the same sentence twice about an arrow; a room holding it beside modulor_man_demo is putting a metre and a canon in the same sightline, which is what the post does in miniature. ON THE VALUE SIDE this family is the corpus's clearest case of one word across incommensurable vocabularies: eleven words, three lists, one shared null under two names, and a second name collision - `body` means 'no apparatus' in modulor_man_demo's `measure` and 'the mass being pushed' in ForceMagnitudeDemo's other axis.
declines: `both` FROM ForceMagnitudeDemo, AND IT IS THE ALL-RUNGS RULE, not a preference. `both` draws velocity AND acceleration together - the branches are `shown == "both" or shown == "velocity"` and `shown == "both" or shown == "acceleration"`, plus a nine-line readout carrying both - so it is a value that contains other values of the same axis. Wave 13's lesson: an all-rungs value inside an axis makes every other value a subset of one cell and cannot be compared with any of them, which is why this bench's `layout` is a separate export pinned by the fixture. `both` breaks the rule in the axis; `ladder` would break it in the layout; neither is allowed in `measure`. It is also, awkwardly, the member's DEFAULT and the state all five of its placements ship in - so the family's most-placed value for this axis is one that cannot be swept.

THE BRIEF'S KIND-ASSIGNMENT, corrected from the code, and it is the biggest change. The brief said ForceMagnitudeDemo's velocity and acceleration are derivatives that do not exist at an instant without a limit, so drawing them requires choosing a time window; that rounded_softbody's strain and volume are state; and that the Modulor's words are a canon. The last two hold. THE FIRST DOES NOT. That file takes no limit anywhere: velocity is read off physics_ball.linear_velocity, the engine's integral, and acceleration is force_logical / _mass, a division. The only difference quotient in four artifacts is in the value the brief filed under state - `collision`, whose vel = (current - prev) / maxf(delta, 0.001) is a finite difference over one physics tick with a 0.5 s decay on the display. So the `window` reading is empty for SIX of eight values rather than the five the brief predicted, and the sixth is the one named after a derivative. The bench is built the same way under either reading; the note and the nulls now say which is true.

THE BRIEF'S GUESS THAT THE TWO SOFTBODY NAMES ARE ONE SCENE, corrected in a specific direction. They are two scenes, nested: rounded_softbody_test.tscn instances rounded_softbody.tscn as the child `RoundedSoftBody` and adds a floor and a collider, and its root script is a pass-through that owns nothing, builds nothing, draws nothing, re-declares the same four-value enum character for character and forwards config down. So it is ONE IMPLEMENTATION under two names rather than one scene, and the second name exists because the first was unreachable - the harness root used to carry no script, so GridInteractablesComponent's apply_grid_config call on the ROOT fell through for all eight placements. Both are listed in `sources` because both are real registry tokens with real placements, but they contribute ONE vocabulary, not two, and the family's census is three vocabularies across four names.

`scale` FROM modulor_man_demo, AND IT IS DECLINED BECAUSE THIS BENCH ALREADY IS IT. The member's `scale` builds a graduated rule standing beside the figure with a tick at every Red-series height and the scene's ten dimension labels turned on. The invariant rail here is a graduated rule standing beside the body, present in all twenty-four cells - so `scale` as a value would draw the bench's own instrument a second time, and every pair involving it would be measuring a duplicate. Promoting it to the stage instead is the honest move: it says that a graduated metre is not one measure among eight, it is what the other seven are read against.

`crowd` FROM modulor_man_demo, on extent. It stands four more figures in a rank at 0.74 m pitch starting at x = 1.02 - at 1:2 that is x = 0.51 to 1.62, three times the plate's half-width - and the whole point of the value is that the rank runs out past the standard. Capping it would delete the argument; building it would take the framing with it and photograph everything else as a speck, which is the granular lesson from wave 18 in a worse form. It is the best value in the member's vocabulary and the one this bench cannot hold. If the axis ever gets a ninth value, it should be this one, on a wider stage built for it.

`body` FROM modulor_man_demo, as a duplicate of `none`. Its branch is `if measure == "body" ...: return` before the host node exists - it builds nothing at all, which is exactly what the softbody's `none` does. Two names for one value, and keeping both would put a designed null in the axis by accident rather than by design. `none` is kept because two of the four members use that word. The collision is recorded rather than smoothed over: `body` is ALSO the name of ForceMagnitudeDemo's second axis, where it means the mass being pushed, so the family uses one word for 'no apparatus' and for 'the thing the apparatus is about'.

THE SOFTBODY'S VOLUME STRIP CHART, which is a 120-frame history plotted as a line - VOLUME_HISTORY_SIZE frames of ratio against a target, in three deviation colours. It is the member's best drawing and it is a TIME SERIES, which a still cannot show: one frame of it is one point, and five variants of it are five identical charts, which is the info_board fault from the wave-13 notes. The volume cubes replace it. What is kept is the member's arithmetic, its deviation thresholds and its three colours, applied to a length instead of to a plot.

THE COLLISION DECAY WINDOW, 0.5 s, flagged rather than drawn. The softbody decays each marker at `_collision_decay[i] -= delta * 2.0` and fades its alpha with it, so a collision arrow is visible for half a second after the event. That is a second and different window - a display window on top of the tick-length measurement window - and it is a duration, invisible to a still. The `window` reading draws the measurement window only, and the note says which one is missing.

ANY SIMULATION AT ALL, and it is a larger refusal here than in most syntheses. rounded_softbody runs a real SoftBody3D through PhysicsServer3D every frame and awaits two process frames before it can record a rest state; ForceMagnitudeDemo applies a central force in _physics_process and reads the ball's position back out. Either would put a different mesh in every tile - the sculpt_one fault, where an unseeded generator made five variants into five objects. The squeeze here is a closed-form displacement field on constants, so `strain` and `volume` are measuring one fixed deformation rather than a moment in a simulation. WHAT THAT COSTS is named rather than hidden: the strain field is not a solved elastic field, it is a plausible arithmetic dent, and the number it produces (peak displacement 0.07494 m, E_max 0.00140) is not a physical prediction. What IS derived from the code is the LAW the drawing obeys - 0.5 * k * d^2 with k = 0.5, sz = 0.008 + t * 0.012, t normalised by a running maximum - and that law is the thing the bench is about.

EMISSION, which every one of modulor_man_demo's constructions uses (_lit() with emission_energy_multiplier from 0.42 to 1.6, on the datum lines, the canon frame, the rule and the crowd's datum). The critic measures luminance, and an emissive value separates pairs by glow rather than by geometry - on a bench whose entire argument is about lengths, that would let a bright value beat a long one. Every material here is a plain vertex-coloured StandardMaterial3D with CULL_DISABLED, and the members' colours are carried in the vertices instead.

A LARGER BODY, OR A WIDER PLATE. The plate is 1.00 m across because the longest rod is 0.660 m and the body's face is at x = -0.160, so acceleration lands exactly on the edge. A wider plate would make every pair read cooler by growing the crop; a bigger body would push the acceleration rod off it. The one place this bites is the closest registered pair, which is small partly because the frame is generous - and shrinking the frame to flatter it would be choosing the number over the argument.
dna.sweep_note: THE FULL SHEET NEEDS --max=24 AND THE COST OF GETTING IT WRONG IS THE WHOLE ARGUMENT. `measure` is declared first and is never trimmed; `reading` is second, and build_dna_gallery trims the LATER axis from the tail until the cross product fits its cap. At the default --max=9 the 8 x 3 sheet renders as 8 x 1 = `on` only, which deletes every designed null, the entire window argument and the one finding this bench exists for, and leaves a finished-looking sheet of eight tiles that cannot be wrong about anything. At --max=16 it renders 8 x 2 = on and alone, which keeps the length comparison and still deletes all five nulls. Only 24 carries the experiment. Read the per-pair rows in sweep_measure_bench_bite.json rather than the headline: the headline will be a peak from a pair like acceleration-against-none in `on` at roughly 10 percent, and a live axis hiding a dead one is exactly what a two-axis sweep does when nobody reads the rows.
